## Marking of assignments

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column}

**Essays**

* Two examiners 
* Single joint report
* Blinded

**Dissertations**

* Two examiners 
* Independent reports 
* Not blinded

::::

:::: {.column}

::: {.fragment}

**External examiners**

* Sample focuses on:
   * Particularly high and low
   * Divergent initial marks
* Review for:
   * Soundness and fairness of process
   * Consistency and appropriateness of marking
* Can only advise, not change marks

:::

::::

:::::

## Marking scheme

* Distinction: ≥ 75
* Pass mark: 60
* Marginal pass: 60 – 62 (viva possible)
* Marginal fail:  57 – 59 (viva likely)
* Outright fail: ≤ 56 (viva mandatory)

> An assignment mark between 57 and 59 is considered a marginal fail. This may be compensated by a strong performance in one of the other assignments. This is normally denoted by a mark of 68 or above.

## Overall weighting


* Unit 1: Three essays (45%)
   * Criminological Theories (15%)
   * Optional course 1 (15%)
   * Optional course 2 (15%)
* Unit 2: Criminological Research Methods Portfolio (20%)
* Unit 3: Dissertation (35%)

> To be awarded the MPhil degree you should pass each assignment (i.e. achieve a mark of 60 or above) and achieve an overall weighted mark of 60 or above for the course... To be awarded a **course distinction**, you would be expected to obtain an overall weighted mark of **75**.

## Examination review

* Discuss feedback with supervisor 
* Use **Examination Review Procedure** within 28 days of results
* Grounds for review 
   * *Procedural irregularity* 
   * *Demonstrable bias*
   * *Withdrawal of academic provision* (e.g., strikes)
* Disagreement with the academic judgement of examiners is *not grounds for review*.

# Academic misconduct



## Definition

&nbsp;

> Gaining or attempting to gain, or helping others to gain or attempt to gain, an unfair academic advantage in formal University assessment, or any activity likely to undermine the integrity essential to scholarship and research. 

## Forms

* Plagiarism
   * Whether verbatim, mosaic, or paraphrased
* Self-plagiarism
   * E.g., re-using past work without citation
* Contract cheating
* Collusion
* Impersonation
* Fabrication, falsification or misrepresentation of data, results or other aspects of research
   * This includes work by *others*

## Artificial intelligence

&nbsp;

> A student using any unacknowledged content generated by artificial intelligence within a summative assessment as though it is their own work constitutes academic misconduct, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the assessment brief

AI includes but is not limited to:

* Chat interfaces such as ChatGPT and Claude
* In-application tools like Gemini for Google Docs and Grammarly
* Agents like Claude Cowork or GitHub Copilot

## Using AI

::: {style="font-size: 75%;"}

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
tribble(~`Useful`, ~ `Acceptable (but error prone)`, ~Misconduct,
        "Suggest and explain computer code or equations", "Rephrase or summarize text for your own use", "Rephrase or summarize literature for use in an essay or article",
        "Systematically extract information from text data", "Get writing suggestions, including ways to simplify or condense", "Write passages, essays, or discussion questions for you",
        "Identify features in large numbers of images", "Explain substantive or theoretical ideas for your understanding", "Conduct analyses for you in summative assignments",
        "Generate data (e.g., text, images, sound) for use in experiments", "Translate text or computer code between languages", "Do just about anything without saying you used it"
) |> knitr::kable()
```

:::

::: {.center}

<br>*Ask before using AI tools and always report when using them*

:::

## Three key points

&nbsp;

Intentionality

> Intent is not necessary for actions to constitute misconduct

Responsibility

> Not knowing or forgetting about the rules or their consequences is not a justification for not following them. 

Clarity of authorship

> The Examiners must be left in no doubt as to which parts of any submission are your own original work and which are not

## Possible sanctions

&nbsp;

* An educative session on academic integrity 
* Written reflection 
* An apology 
* Mark for assessment of part of the assignment not affected by misconduct 
* Mark of 0 for the assignment
* Referral to OSCCA and Discipline Committee
